results.name: Parcel_Correction
results.title: Parcel Adjustment for Sandy Springs
results.description:
Overview

This feature service supports a parcel adjustment project for the Sandy Springs area using parcel and subdivision reference layers. It brings together parcel polygons, parcel boundary and centerline support features, parcel identification and annotation content, and subdivision records used to maintain corrected parcel geometry and associated reference information.

Feature Layers

  • Adjusted Parcels provides parcel polygons with ownership, assessment, address, land use, subdivision, and update information used to support corrected parcel records.
  • Parcel Lines and Soft Lines contain parcel boundary linework and curve-related attributes that help represent adjusted parcel geometry.
  • Centerlines provides a minimal line layer used as part of the parcel adjustment dataset structure.
  • PIN stores parcel identification features and related parcel reference details such as acreage, plat, deed, and recording information.
  • Subdivisions contains subdivision names and plat references that support parcel indexing and adjustment workflows.
  • Annotation Points stores text annotation elements used to place labels and parcel-related annotation content.

Geographic Coverage

The service covers a local parcel adjustment area for Sandy Springs in Fulton County, Georgia.

Use Cases

  • Maintaining corrected parcel boundaries and related parcel reference layers
  • Supporting parcel review and update workflows from recorded plats and surveys
  • Displaying parcel identifiers, subdivision references, and label placement for cartographic products
  • Providing local parcel editing support for GIS applications and web mapping

Data Stewardship

Recorded plats and surveys are incorporated into the adjustment workflow on a recurring basis. Fulton County remains the authoritative source for parcel data.
results.snippet: Parcel adjustment layers supporting corrected parcel boundaries, parcel identifiers, subdivision references, and annotation content for Sandy Springs, Georgia. Recorded plats and surveys are incorporated regularly, while Fulton County remains the authoritative parcel source.

results.description: This dataset represents the boundary of each parcel of land in Fulton County recorded for the pupose of aiding in the appraisal of real property and the determination of property tax. A parcel dataset is created each year in association with that year's tax digest. The parcel dataset for any given year is not considered final until the completion of the digest, which generally occurs around mid-year. Until the completion of the digest, the parcel dataset is considered to be a work in progress. Any necessary corrections and omissions may continue to be made even after the completion of the digest. The parcel dataset in its published form incorporates information from the CAMA (computer-aided mass appraisal) database. The CAMA information included with the published dataset is selected based on its value to the typical consumer of the data and includes the parcel identification number, the property address, property owner, owner's mailing address, tax district, assessed and appraised value for land and improvements, the number of livable units, acreage, property class and land use class. The information in this data set represents the completed 2019 digest.

results.description: This data layer is an Esri file geodatabase polygon feature class that contains parcel boundaries maintained by county agencies in Indiana. It was released by the Indiana Geographic Information Office (IGIO) on February 1, 2022. The IGIO compiled the data as part of the Indiana Data Harvest program between the Indiana Geographic Information Council (IGIC) and all Indiana counties to provide the most accurate framework data for the citizens of Indiana. results.name: Tear_Down_Analysis
results.title: Tear Down Analysis
results.description:
As Atlanta continues to rapidly grow, neighborhoods are changing. One phenomenon that is anecdotally observable in the city is the construction of large homes in existing neighborhoods. To quantify this phenomenon, this analysis uses data from the City of Atlanta's Accela database to match tax parcels where single family demolition permits were issued and subsequently followed by a new single family construction permit between 2010-2020. We then analyzed tax data from these parcels to show how the Improvement Appraisal value changed at various intervals: year-to-year, 2010-2015, 2015-2020, and 2010-2020. The Improvement Appraisal signifies the appraised value of the improvements on a parcel where improvements refer to built structures rather than the value of the land itself. Thus our analysis tracks changes in value related to the homes themselves as they are torn down and rebuilt. 

SUMMARY OF FINDINGS

There are several interesting findings observable in the data and displayed in the related Story Map that uses these layers:

  • 4,367 single family residential demolition permits were issued between 2010-2020. 6,597 new SF construction permits were issued in that same time period. 2,393 parcels were demolished and then rebuilt. This means that

     

    • 55% of all demolition permits resulted in new construction.
    • 36% of all new single family construction permits followed a demolition.

     

    These tear downs/rebuilds resulted in significant returns for property owners:

     

    • 30% of tear downs (714 parcels) saw improvement appraisal value increases of over 500% between 2010-2020.

    • 68% of tear downs (1,637 parcels) saw improvement appraisal value increases of at least 100% between 2010-2020.



NOTES ABOUT THE DATA

  • To build this Story Map we used the City of Atlanta's Accela database to match tax parcels where single family demolition permits were issued and subsequently followed by a new single family construction permit between 2010-2020. We then analyzed tax data from these parcels to show how the improvement appraisal value changed at various intervals: year-to-year, 2010-2015, 2015-2020, and 2010-2020. The improvement appraisal refers to the value of built structures rather than the value of the land itself. Thus our analysis in the Fulton County portions of the City tracks changes in value related to the homes themselves as they are torn down and rebuilt. As previously noted, our analysis in the Dekalb portions only analyze total appraisal value for three years: 2010,2015, and 2020. 

     

    Lastly, data on the changes in square footage through the tear down process is not reliably available. During the permit intake process, square footage is either not always recorded or is recorded but cannot be due to the way Accela produces reports.
results.snippet: This map shows tax parcels where a demolition permit was issued for a single family home, followed by a subsequent new single family construction permit. The data tracks these tear downs and rebuilds from 2010-2020 for the Fulton County portion of the City of Atlanta only.
results.source: City of Atlanta - Department of City Planning GIS

results.description:
CountyParcels_DLGF_RESTRICTED is an enhanced version of County Parcel data collected from each of the 92 counties in Indiana as part of the Indiana Data Sharing Initiative (IDSI). These data include the parcel features and attributes from assessment data provided to the Department of Local Government and Finance. Please note, there may be records with duplicate parcel IDs. That will result in the DLGF information being duplicated for each record. The owner, class code, etc. will still be correct, but the value and deeded acreage fields will be for the sum of the matched numbers, not the individual polygons. IMPORTANT: All records in this dataset are completely replaced with each update. Therefore, using the "Create Layer from Selected Features" in ArcMap will not work correctly after the proceeding update, nor will definition queries based on OBJECTID.

Latest update: 11/7/2019 with 2019 polygons (GIO.COUNTY_Parcel) and 2018 pay 2019 DLGF information.
